Well, I think that from what I can tell, I'm talking to producers, they still are in the mentality that some aren't other. The government is going to take care of all the places. When you go into the banker, you can look at their balance sheet and so forth, decide What kind of guarantee they need to have underneath their income? Is that $650 above feed cost? Is it $550? I think it's a big mistake for those producers not to buy that kind of coverage in case we have a collapse. Should there be work now in the SNAP program? Or should they just be considered to bring the change, not until the next Farm Bill?

Well, I'm a guest opening the Farm Bill and making changes in SNAP. It's opening the Farm Bill, which so I'm not familiar with that. Some of the emphasis has been placed on this program. It's frankly been putting the emphasis in the wrong area of where policy should be examined. You know, 80% of the people on SNAP couldn't work if you wanted them. Their children, their elderly, they're disabled. And all this focus has been on work requirements. And, you know, we made changes back a long time ago that you could only be on these welfare programs, including SNAP, if it's three months, if you're not working or not meeting your requirements to find work. But the problem is we put waivers in the law that allow a lot of areas where there are no jobs and a lot of people on SNAP. We've allowed them to waive all the law. So you have these abods. able-bodied people on SNAP because we gave the governor the city's the authority to wave out at us. So, you know, that's one thing that should be looked at. The other thing is this categorical eligibility, which allows states to set the income threshold that you qualify for SNAP, the federal threshold is 130%. A number of states are set thresholds above that. And we've allowed the states to use that extensively for simplicity. So you have a situation where the states can qualify people for SNAP and they send a bill to the federal government that they don't pay any for it. You know, that's a dumb idea. You know, and I tried during the farm bill to have people to address this. You know, we have 130% threshold. So in a lot of states, If you're above 100% of poverty, you cannot qualify for SNAP. But in, you know, like in my state of Minnesota, it's 165%. In Texas, it's 165%. In some states, North Dakota and Arizona, it's 200%. So you have a situation where some people like in Fargo qualify and people in Market don't for the same income level. That's where the focus should be, in my opinion, on the policy changes, if any, that are made in snap. But I don't think we should do that until the next learn bill.
